sections.title: VectorX
sections.subtitle: Code scanning and supply-chain analysis, repo to release.

sections.heading: Software security from repo to release
sections.body: VectorX is for engineering and security teams reviewing code change and software supply-chain risk before release. It brings code scanning and supply-chain analysis into the repository-to-release assurance conversation.
sections.secondaryHeading: Connect findings to a release decision
sections.secondaryBody:
Evaluate the product using a representative repository change and the evidence your team needs to review it. VectorX is part of our [Cyber Security](/services/cyber-security) portfolio; optional services can help define assurance responsibilities and adoption.

[Request a VectorX demo](#get-in-touch) · [Browse products](/products-and-accelerators)

sections.heading: Review code and its software supply chain
sections.description: Repo to release describes the workflow, not a separate scan type. Confirm pipeline and reporting capabilities against your development estate.

items.title: Code scanning
items.description: Inspect how a representative change is scanned and how findings are presented. Confirm supported scan types and languages rather than assume a particular test category.

items.title: Supply-chain analysis
items.description: Review the product’s analysis of the software supply chain. Confirm supported dependency and package ecosystems, coverage boundaries and the evidence produced.

sections.heading: From repository change to release review
sections.description: Illustrative evaluation workflow: repository change → analysis → finding review → release decision. This is not a product-interface demonstration.

items.title: Scope a representative change
items.description: Select a repository and release workflow. Agree code access, scan location, supported technologies and the evaluation boundary.

items.title: Scan and review findings
items.description: Walk through code scanning and supply-chain analysis. Ask the engineering and security owners to review the finding evidence and its limitations.

items.title: Decide and retain evidence
items.description: Agree triage, remediation ownership and the release decision. Confirm how supported outputs connect with your pipeline and issue-handling process.

sections.heading: Example: assurance for AI-written change
sections.body:
An engineering team is introducing AI-generated code and needs a review path before release. Evaluate VectorX code and supply-chain analysis against a representative change, with developers and security owners assessing the resulting evidence.

This illustrative pattern is not a client result and does not establish scan coverage or an automatic release gate.
sections.secondaryBody:
[AI Code Assurance](/solutions/ai-code-assurance) connects VectorX, testoriumz and Cyber-Safe Delivery with quality and security gates across CI/CD. Functional testing and security analysis answer different questions; agree their hand-off in your workflow.

[Quality engineering services](/services/digital-transformation/quality-engineering) can support the testing approach. Product licences and optional services are scoped separately.

sections.heading: Enterprise fit and licensing
sections.description: Agree the supported estate, operating responsibilities and commercial scope before selecting VectorX.

items.title: Deployment and integrations
items.description: Confirm supported repositories, languages, package managers and scan categories, plus CI/CD and issue-tracking integrations. Establish scan location, access requirements and available deployment options during evaluation.

items.title: Security and responsibility
items.description: Review repository permissions, code transfer, retention and evidence access. Clarify tenant boundaries, data handling and the responsibilities of the product operator, engineering team and security reviewer.

items.title: Licence and optional services
items.description: Available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without Linkfields services. Confirm current availability, onboarding, support and commercial scope in a guided discussion; no public trial is assumed.

sections.note: Licence and subscription describe buying terms; they do not establish which hosting options are available. Confirm deployment, support and inclusion details for your scope.
